items.title: Boeing vs. Space Exploration Technologies: Which Flight Giant Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Boeing's turnaround is real, but its debt load and negative free cash flow raise questions. SpaceX burns cash aggressively yet commands a large forward P/E.

items.title: Space Weapons: How Boeing, SpaceX, and Others Stand to Gain
items.summary: On Monday, the U.S. Space Force confirmed the existence of space-based weapons, though what exactly is in space is classified.  The news represents a milestone in military technology.  Space is the new strategic high ground.

items.title: Boeing vs. Redwire: Which Aerospace Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Boeing's 35% revenue surge masks a negative free cash flow and 10x debt load, while Redwire burns cash but carries minimal leverage, a classic risk-reward trade-off.

items.title: Pentagon Adds $13.4 Billion to Boeing (BA) Contract. That Isn’t an Immediate Financial Windfall
items.summary: The Pentagon has expanded the potential value of Boeing’s KC-46 Pegasus Combat Capability contract by $13.4 billion. That more than triples the contract’s ceiling from $5.7 billion to $19.1 billion. The Pentagon has also expanded the agreement to include Foreign Military Sales (FMS). items.summary: On August 14, the Pentagon announced framework agreements with The Boeing Company (NYSE:BA) and RTX Corporation (NYSE:RTX) to increase component production for the SM-3 Block IIA and SM-3 Block IB interceptors. items.title: 2 Reasons to Like BA and 1 to Stay Skeptical
items.summary: Boeing has been treading water for the past six months, recording a small loss of 1.5% while holding steady at $210.29. The stock also fell short of the S&P 500’s 14.2% gain during that period.

items.title: Surging Oil Prices Singe GE Aerospace
items.summary: Soaring oil prices are hurting shares of once high-flying aviation suppliers, with engine maker GE Aerospace suffering the brunt of the selloff. Its shares were down about 3% midday at $308.50, extending a nearly weeklong slump for the manufacturer.

items.title: Why Is Boeing Stock Falling While Revenue Soars Past Peers?
items.summary: Boeing (BA) grew revenue faster over the past twelve months than any of its aerospace and defense peers, GE Aerospace included, and its stock still fell. It is also the only one in that group running an operating loss. The growth has come with rising airplane deliveries, and the market is waiting to see whether those airplanes earn a margin.
